    private static function portFor(array $parts): int
    {
        return $parts['port'] ?? ($parts['scheme'] === 'https' ? 443 : 80);
    }

    /**
     * @return array{
     *     scheme: string,
     *     host: string,
     *     port?: int
     * }
     */
    private function validateUrl(string $url): array
    {
        if ($url === '') {
            throw new InvalidArgumentException(
                'A download URL is required.'
            );
        }

        if (strlen($url) > 8192) {
            throw new InvalidArgumentException(
                'The download URL is too long.'
            );
        }

        $parts = parse_url($url);

        if ($parts === false) {
            throw new InvalidArgumentException(
                'The download URL is invalid.'
            );
        }

        $scheme = strtolower((string) ($parts['scheme'] ?? ''));

        if (!in_array($scheme, ['http', 'https'], true)) {
            throw new InvalidArgumentException(
                'Only HTTP and HTTPS download URLs are allowed.'
            );
        }

        $host = $parts['host'] ?? '';

        if (str_starts_with($host, '[') && str_ends_with($host, ']')) {
            $host = substr($host, 1, -1);
        }

        if ($host === '') {
            throw new InvalidArgumentException(
                'The download URL must contain a host.'
            );
        }

        if (isset($parts['user']) || isset($parts['pass'])) {
            throw new InvalidArgumentException(
                'Download URLs cannot contain credentials.'
            );
        }

        if (isset($parts['port'])) {
            $port = (int) $parts['port'];

            if ($port < 1 || $port > 65535) {
                throw new InvalidArgumentException(
                    'The download URL contains an invalid port.'
                );
            }

            return [
                'scheme' => $scheme,
                'host' => $host,
                'port' => $port,
            ];
        }

        return [
            'scheme' => $scheme,
            'host' => $host,
        ];
    }

    /**
     * Builds CURLOPT_RESOLVE entries for every verified public IPv4 address of
     * the download host. Pinning several addresses (instead of a single
     * resolved IP) lets libcurl fail over between CDN edges, which prevents a
     * single throttled or flaky edge from aborting a large transfer.
     *
     * IPv6 (AAAA) addresses are deliberately not pinned. When libcurl is given
     * a bond for an address family the host cannot route, it aborts the whole
     * connect instead of falling back to the pinned IPv4 address, so dual
     * stack hosts are pinned by their IPv4 addresses only.
     *
     * @param array{scheme: string, host: string, port?: int} $parts
     *
     * @return list<string>
     */
    private function resolveEntries(array $parts): array
    {
        $entries = [];

        foreach ($this->resolvePublicAddresses($parts['host']) as $ip) {
            $entries[] = $parts['host']
                . ':' . self::portFor($parts)
                . ':' . $ip;
        }

        return $entries;
    }

    /**
     * Resolves a host to its verified public addresses, preferring IPv4.
     *
     * @return list<string>
     */
    private function resolvePublicAddresses(string $host): array
    {
        if (filter_var($host, FILTER_VALIDATE_IP)) {
            $this->assertPublicAddress($host);

            return [$host];
        }

        $records = dns_get_record(
            $host,
            DNS_A | DNS_AAAA,
        );

        if ($records === false || $records === []) {
            throw new InvalidArgumentException(
                'Unable to resolve the download host.'
            );
        }

        $ipv4 = [];
        $ipv6 = [];

        foreach ($records as $record) {
            $ip = $record['ip'] ?? $record['ipv6'] ?? null;

            if ($ip === null) {
                continue;
            }

            try {
                $this->assertPublicAddress($ip);
            } catch (InvalidArgumentException) {
                continue;
            }

            if (str_contains($ip, ':')) {
                $ipv6[$ip] = true;
            } else {
                $ipv4[$ip] = true;
            }
        }

        if ($ipv4 !== []) {
            return array_keys($ipv4);
        }

        if ($ipv6 !== []) {
            return array_keys($ipv6);
        }

        throw new InvalidArgumentException(
            'The download host resolves only to private or reserved addresses.'
        );
    }

    /**
     * Writes a structured diagnostic line before a transfer failure is
     * rethrown so production panels can see exactly which curl error killed
     * the download instead of only a generic "Unable to install the modpack".
     */
    private function recordTransferFailure(
        $curl,
        string $host,
        string $url,
    ): void {
        $expected = curl_getinfo($curl, CURLINFO_CONTENT_LENGTH_DOWNLOAD);

        $details = [
            'event' => 'download_failure',
            'errno' => curl_errno($curl),
            'error' => trim((string) curl_error($curl)),
            'host' => $host,
            'has_query' => parse_url($url, PHP_URL_QUERY) !== false,
            'http_status' => (int) curl_getinfo($curl, CURLINFO_RESPONSE_CODE),
            'downloaded_bytes' => (int) curl_getinfo($curl, CURLINFO_SIZE_DOWNLOAD),
            'expected_bytes' => $expected >= 0 ? (int) $expected : null,
            'speed_bytes_per_second' => (int) curl_getinfo($curl, CURLINFO_SPEED_DOWNLOAD),
            'elapsed_seconds' => round((float) curl_getinfo($curl, CURLINFO_TOTAL_TIME), 2),
            'disk_free_bytes' => $this->temporaryDiskFree(),
            'memory_used_bytes' => memory_get_usage(true),
            'memory_peak_bytes' => memory_get_peak_usage(true),
            'memory_limit' => ini_get('memory_limit'),
            'php_version' => PHP_VERSION,
        ];

        @error_log(
            'modpackinstaller download failure: '
            . (string) json_encode($details)
        );

        @error_log(
            'modpackinstaller download failure (human readable): '
            . 'errno=' . (string) $details['errno']
            . ' host=' . $host
            . ' status=' . (string) $details['http_status']
            . ' downloaded=' . (string) $details['downloaded_bytes']
            . ' expected=' . (string) ($details['expected_bytes'] ?? -1)
            . ' disk_free=' . (string) ($details['disk_free_bytes'] ?? -1)
            . ' memory_limit=' . (string) $details['memory_limit']
            . ' memory_used=' . (string) $details['memory_used_bytes']
            . ' error_message=' . (string) $details['error']
        );
    }

    private function temporaryDiskFree(): ?int
    {
        $free = @disk_free_space($this->temporaryRoot);

        return $free === false ? null : (int) $free;
    }

    private function assertPublicAddress(string $ip): void
    {
        if (
            filter_var(
                $ip,
                FILTER_VALIDATE_IP,
                FILTER_FLAG_NO_PRIV_RANGE | FILTER_FLAG_NO_RES_RANGE,
            ) === false
        ) {
            throw new InvalidArgumentException(
                'The download host resolves to a private or reserved address.'
            );
        }

        foreach (self::BLOCKED_CIDRS as $cidr) {
            if ($this->inCidr($ip, $cidr)) {
                throw new InvalidArgumentException(
                    'The download host resolves to a private or reserved address.'
                );
            }
        }
    }

    private function inCidr(string $ip, string $cidr): bool
    {
        [$network, $prefix] = array_pad(explode('/', $cidr), 2, null);

        if ($prefix === null || !is_numeric($prefix)) {
            return false;
        }

        $prefix = (int) $prefix;

        $packedIp = @inet_pton($ip);
        $packedNetwork = @inet_pton($network);

        if ($packedIp === false || $packedNetwork === false) {
            return false;
        }

        $bytes = strlen($packedNetwork);

        $fullBytes = intdiv($prefix, 8);
        $remainingBits = $prefix % 8;

        for ($index = 0; $index < $bytes; $index++) {
            if ($index < $fullBytes) {
                if ($packedIp[$index] !== $packedNetwork[$index]) {
                    return false;
                }

                continue;
            }

            if ($remainingBits === 0) {
                continue;
            }

            $mask = chr(0xFF << (8 - $remainingBits));

            if (
                ($packedIp[$index] & $mask) !== ($packedNetwork[$index] & $mask)
            ) {
                return false;
            }

            break;
        }

        return true;
    }

    private function ensureTemporaryRoot(): void
    {
        if (
            !is_dir($this->temporaryRoot)
            && !mkdir($this->temporaryRoot, 0750, true)
            && !is_dir($this->temporaryRoot)
        ) {
            throw new RuntimeException(
                'Unable to create the temporary download directory.'
            );
        }
    }
}

<?php

namespace Pterodactyl\BlueprintFramework\Extensions\modpackinstaller\Services\Download;

interface Downloader
{
    /**
     * Downloads a remote archive into a secure temporary file.
     *
     * @throws \InvalidArgumentException When the URL is unsafe or invalid.
     * @throws \RuntimeException          When the download fails.
     */
    public function download(string $url): string;

    /**
     * Anchors progress reporting to a running total shared across several
     * downloads. The completed count must keep rising across every download
     * in the batch so callers observe a monotonic, cumulative progress bar.
     *
     * @param int      $completedBytes Bytes completed by *earlier* downloads.
     * @param int|null $totalBytes     Grand total for the whole batch, or null
     *                                 to fall back to per-download reporting.
     */
    public function setProgressOffset(int $completedBytes, ?int $totalBytes): void;

    /**
     * Returns whether the configured cancel predicate currently fires, so
     * callers can abort long-running composition steps (packaging, scrubbing)
     * even when no transfer is actively in flight.
     */
    public function isCancelled(): bool;
}

Now I have a full picture. Let me also quickly check the `installationSource`/`install` entry to confirm which download phase the user is in and confirm the deploy progress. But I have enough.

Let me now design the fix concretely.

## The problem, precisely

After the client pack archive hits 617/617 MB (100% of that single download), the code re-anchors cumulative progress (offset=617MB, total=617MB+mods), then in `buildServerArchive`:

1. For each content entry that is an **override** (`archiveEntry !== null`): copies the entry from the client zip to a scratch `.bin`, then `addFile` to the output zip. **No progress callback is fired** → the store keeps the last `617/617, 84%` snapshot.
2. For each mod: `downloadBestUrl` → `setProgressOffset(networkBytesDone, total)` then `download()`. When a mod has bytes streaming, the XFERINFO fires → progress updates and exceeds 617. **BUT** if the pack mostly has overrides and few/no mods (or mods that fail-skip), progress stays frozen.
3. `$output->close()`: ZipArchive **deflates every entry** (default compression) — reading each scratch file and compressing, potentially hundreds of MB — with **no cancel check and no progress**. This is the "forever" that swallows Cancel.

So even with my earlier fixes, `$output->addFile()` + `$output->close()` remain a fully non-cancellable, non-progress-reporting, CPU/IO-heavy phase. The user observes exactly this: frozen bar + cancel ignored until my frontend 90s kill-switch fired.

## Fix design

Replace the "copy-to-scratch then addFile then deflate-on-close" pipeline with a **direct streaming write of STORED entries** into the output archive that:
- mirrors each content entry once (no scratch double-write),
- checks `isCancelled()` per 256 KB chunk,
- reports cumulative progress per chunk (so the bar moves during override copies too),
- computes CRC32 + sizes incrementally and patches the local headers at `close()`,
- writes the central directory at close (fast, bounded).

This removes the deferred deflate entirely (STORED = no compression → close() is trivial), removes the scratch files, and makes the whole phase cancellable and progress-visible.

### Required supporting change: a public progress-reporter on the Downloader

The provider needs to push progress during override copies (no curl involved). Add `reportProgress(int $downloadBytes, ?int $totalBytes)`? Hmm. Let me think about the cleanest API within the existing design.

The DownloadManager already centralizes the progress callback + offset logic. I'll add:

```php
public function reportProgress(int $downloadedBytes): void
```

Semantics: interpret `$downloadedBytes` as the current transfer's cumulative bytes, exactly like the XFERINFO handler does — i.e., combine with `progressOffsetBytes` when `progressOffsetTotal` is set, throttle by 0.4s, invoke the callback. That keeps the controller's clamping/monotonic logic working identically. The throttling also matters because the provider will call it per chunk.

So:
- During override entry streaming, call `reportProgress($copiedBytes)` where `$copiedBytes` is bytes copied for the *current entry* (0..entrySize). Because the offset was anchored at the client-pack size, `reportProgress` computes `done = offset + copied` → moves the bar as overrides are processed. Wait, but offset stays at 617MB throughout all entries. As we copy overrides, `copied` grows per entry to entry size, and resets each entry → `done` oscillates? No — it's monotonic only if each entry's `copied` grows from 0 upward, and the controller clamps with `max($lastPercent, ...)`. Consider entry1 = 400MB, entry2 = 200MB, entry3 = 300MB. Offset = 617. 
  - entry1: done goes 617→617+400=1017. Clamped upward. lastPercent rises.
  - entry2: done goes 617→617+200=817 < 1017 → clamp keeps lastPercent. Bar doesn't move DOWN (monotonic), stays at last.
  - entry3: done goes 617→617+300=917 < 1017 → stays at last.
  - Net: bar moves to 1017=client+400MB, then freezes during the rest. Not ideal but acceptable? The total `archiveBytes` = client(617) + sum(mod bytes). If mods are few, archiveBytes≈617+small; then 1017 could EXCEED archiveBytes → min() caps at archiveBytes... done=1017, total=700 → ratio=1.0 → percent=85. That'd jump to 85 (max download). Then deploy continues.

  That's inconsistent. The offset semantically represents "network bytes already done" = client pack size. Override bytes come FROM the client pack, so counting the client pack once covers them. If mods total only e.g. 80MB, total=697. done for entry1 reaches 617(client)+400(override copied) = 1017 → clamped to 697. Bar hits 85%. Slightly misleading but monotonic and moving. Meh.

  Better semantics: after the client pack archive is downloaded (617), and BEFORE entering the loop, set `reportProgress` to advance a "composition progress" that counts the *content we've already got* (client pack + successfully-completed downloads) plus current entry's copied bytes — i.e., make override copies count toward the archive total. The cleanest isn't worth over-engineering. The KEY user need is: bar moves and cancel works. The exact percentage fidelity during the packaging phase matters less; percent is capped at 85 until >85 anyway (85 is download max).

  Actually wait — there's a subtle monotonicity interplay with the mod downloads. In `downloadBestUrl`, `setProgressOffset($networkBytesDone, archiveBytes)` then `download()` — the XFERINFO reports `offset + downloadedModBytes` where offset increments by each mod's `payload['bytes']` after success. Override copies happen between mod downloads in arbitrary order (content is keyed by relative path). If I report override progress with `offset + copiedWithinEntry`, and around the same time mod downloads re-anchor `offset` to a LOWER value (because offset only counts client pack + completed mods; e.g., after 2 mods offset=617+50MB, then an override copy reports offset(667)+copied... then next mod re-anchors to 667+...). The controller clamps monotonic so no dips. Fine.

  Conclusion: `reportProgress(int $downloadedBytes)` that behaves exactly like the mid-transfer callback (offset + downloadedBytes, throttle) is the right API. But to make override progress semantically sensible, I'll track a `$compositionBytes` running counter for non-network work and pass it as the "current download's cumulative bytes within offset"... hmm, the offset already holds client-pack bytes. Actually simplest correct approach: treat override copying as part of the archive's "work done" by reporting `networkBytesDone + archivedWithinArchive` where `archivedWithinArchive` = bytes successfully written to the output so far (cumulative across all entries). Since `networkBytesDone` (offset) = client pack + completed mods, adding cumulative written archive bytes could double count mods (mod bytes are in both). Ugh.

  OK, I'm overthinking the number. The pragmatic approach: for override entries, report `offset + cumulativeBytesWrittenSoFarIncludingThisEntry`. For mod entries, the download's own XFERINFO fires and reports `offset + downloaded`, which is correct and moves the bar; then after success we add mod bytes to offset. Since the controller clamps monotonic, any momentary "float" from double counting is harmless (it's ≤ archiveBytes anyway if we define archiveBytes = client + all mod payloads; override-written bytes push past archiveBytes → capped at 85%).

  Actually, let me define it cleanly to avoid nonsense percentages:

  `archiveBytes` (total) = client pack size + Σ mod file lengths (unchanged).
  `offset` (completed) = client pack size + Σ successfully-downloaded mod lengths (unchanged, updated in downloadBestUrl loop via networkBytesDone).
  
  Override entry progress: report `offsetAtEntryStart + bytesCopiedForThisEntry`, but cap the reported "done" at `archiveBytes`. Since offsetAtEntryStart ≈ client pack + mods done before this entry, and bytesCopied ≤ entry size. If overrides total more than client+mods... it can still exceed total. Cap at total in the callback via existing `min(done, globalTotal)` — already done in the XFERINFO handler! Great: `min($done, $globalTotal)` exists. So reporting `networkBytesDone + copiedWithinEntry` is naturally capped. And because networkBytesDone only grows after mod downloads, and each entry's copied resets, the clamp in the controller keeps it monotonic. Worst case the bar sits at 85% (capped) during the copy-heavy phase — which is EXACTLY right: that's the download/packaging phase at full steam, moving to 'preparing' next.

  Wait, one more: mid-copy of a huge override entry (e.g. 400MB world), `networkBytesDone + copied` grows 617→1017, capped to total (say 697) → percent 85 → monotonic, stays. Bar stuck at 85% now instead of 84% — at least it moved and it's *correct* (85% = download phase complete). And cancel works. Good enough, and honest.

  Hmm — but actually, is it worth ALSO making the packaged-archive bytes report so the bar keeps climbing through the whole packaging (to visually show it "working")? The user explicitly complains it "doesn't move a budge from 84%". If we can make it genuinely reflect the whole packaging pipeline (overrides + mods + zip writing), that's the best UX. Let me consider tracking work more richly... 

  I'll keep it simple and robust: report override progress as above; it guarantees movement + monotonicity + cancellation. The mod downloads already report. This fully addresses "never moves from 84%".

### Rewriting buildServerArchive with a streaming zip writer

I'll write a private method:

```php
private function writeStoredEntry($output, int &$localHeaderOffset, string $relative, int $crc, int $sizeBytes, ...): void
```

Wait — file data must be streamed BEFORE we know CRC/size, but the local file header (with STORE) contains CRC-32 and sizes in the header itself (bit 3 not set for STORE-with-known-sizes... actually the streaming pattern sets general purpose bit 3 = data descriptor present, then writes a data descriptor after data. But many unzip tools require... ZipArchive/php reads it fine). Let me use the **seek-back-and-patch** variant since our output handle is seekable (`fopen('wb+')`):

For each entry:
1. Record `$offset = ftell($output)`.
2. Write a placeholder local file header (version 20, flags 0, method 0 STORE, mtime, crc=0, csize=0, usize=0, name len, extra len 0, name).
3. Save `$crcUpdate = hash_init('crc32b')`, `$usize = 0`, `$csize = 0`.
4. Stream chunks from source → `fwrite($output, $chunk)`; `hash_update($crcUpdate, $chunk)`; `$csize += strlen`; `$usize += strlen`; per-chunk: cancel check + `reportProgress(...)`.
5. After the stream: `$crc = hexdec? ` — `hash_final($crcUpdate)` returns hex string (for crc32b it's an 8-char hex). Convert to int: `hexdec(hash_final($crcUpdate, true))`? No wait — `hash_final(..., true)` returns raw bytes (4 bytes little-endian for crc32b? The raw output of crc32b is the CRC bytes in big-endian order). The zip stores CRC-32 in little-endian. Standard approach: `crc32()` on the whole data gives an int; for chunked we want hash. Compensate: `$crc = unpack('V', hash_final($hash, true))[1];` — `unpack('V', ...)` interprets the 4 bytes as unsigned little-endian int32. Since hash gives big-endian byte order of the CRC value, `unpack('V')` flips to little-endian interpretation... wait. CRC32 value X = 0xAABBCCDD stored big-endian raw = AA BB CC DD. Zip wants LE bytes DD CC BB AA. `unpack('V', "AA BB CC DD")` returns 0xDDCCBBAA = little-endian interpretation of the byte sequence = which is the LE representation of X = same numeric value as crc32()? crc32() returns the CRC as a number computed with standard algorithm; the standard CRC value as an integer is 0xDDCCBBAA (the "reflected" form, endianness aside). Actually PHP's crc32() returns exactly the same number that unpack('V', hash('crc32b', raw, true)) gives — this is a well-known equivalence: `unpack('V', hash('crc32b', $data, true))[1] === crc32($data)` (mod 2^32, and values may be negative int on 32-bit PHP; here 64-bit PHP so fine). Yes, this is the standard recipe. Good.
6. Now patch the local header: seek back to `$offset` and write the same header but with CRC, csizes, usize. Then seek to end. But we know the header structure exactly (fixed+name length), so `fseek($output, $offset + 14, SEEK_SET); fwrite packed crc; fwrite packed csize; fwrite packed usize;` (offsets: 14=crc, 18=csize, 22=usize). Then `fseek($output, 0, SEEK_END)`.
7. Record the central directory entry (relative, crc, csize, usize, headerOffset) in an array for the final central directory.

At the end (`finish`):
- Write central directory: each entry: signature 0x02014b50, version made by (0x031E unix? use 20), version needed (20), flags 0, method 0, time/date, crc, csize, usize, name len, extra 0, comment 0, disk 0, internal attrs 0, external attrs (mode 0644 << 16 | ...), local header offset, name.
- Write EOCD: 0x06054b50, disk counts 0, entries count, cd size, cd offset, comment len 0.

ZIP64: csize/usize could exceed 0xFFFFFFFF for >4GB entries/total; entries here are mod jars/overrides < 4GB each. The 617MB pack unpacked is well under. I'll add a guard: if usize or csize > 0xFFFFFFFF, throw (unsupported by this writer) — but realistically never happens. Actually a world folder entry could theoretically be big but < 4GB in a 617MB zip. Fine.

Version needed: for STORE, 20 suffices (or 10). Use 20.

### Time/date for entries
Zip dos time = now. Compute DOS date/time from `time()`. Standard formula. External attrs: `(0644 << 16)` plus maybe `<< 16` includes mode bits; ZipArchive reads mode. For directories we don't add directory entries (the archive only contains files; extraction creates parent dirs). Wait — original code had only files (collectArchiveContent skips dirs, manifest mods are files). Good.

### CRC chunk math
Use `hash_init('crc32b')`, `hash_update` per chunk. At end, `$crc = unpack('V', hash_final($hash, true))[1];`. hash_final with raw=true returns 4 raw bytes; unpack('V') = unsigned 32-bit LE int. 

### DOS date
```php
$timestamp = time();
$dosTime = (($timestamp % 86400) >> 1) ... 
```
Standard:
```php
$dos = (
    (($year - 1980) << 9)
    | ($month << 5)
    | $day
) << 16 | (($hour << 11) | ($min << 5) | intdiv($sec, 2));
```
where year/month/day/hour/min/sec from localtime or getdate. Use `getdate()`.

### Progress reporting during write
Per chunk (after write), call `$this->downloader->reportProgress($networkBytesDoneAtEntryStart + $usize)` (throttled inside DownloadManager). Hmm but reportProgress uses `progressOffsetTotal` for total. The total was set by `setProgressOffset(networkBytesDone, archiveBytes)` at the top of buildServerArchive. During override entries networkBytesDone isn't changed by the entry, so I need to pass the current entry's base. Let me pass `$baseDone` = current `$networkBytesDone` (which at loop start = client pack size, and grows only in downloadBestUrl). So report = base + usizeSoFar.

Actually simpler: call reportProgress with `$baseDone + $usize` where `$baseDone` is the value of `$networkBytesDone` *at the time this entry's streaming starts*. For mod entries, we don't report via our own writer (the download's XFERINFO reports; but after download completes, `networkBytesDone += modBytes`). During the actual `$output` write of a mod file (which now happens in the same streaming write loop), we'd report `postDownloadNetworkBytesDone + writtenSoFar` — wait, networkBytesDone was already bumped BEFORE we open downloadPath stream (line 883). So for mod entries baseDone = networkBytesDone already including this mod → report = baseDone at loop iteration + written. Good, still monotonic-ish and capped.

Note after a mod download succeeds, downloadBestUrl re-anchored offset inside download()? No: `setProgressOffset` was called BEFORE download, and download uses it; after download returns, provider increments `networkBytesDone` by payload bytes (line 883-886) — but does NOT call setProgressOffset again with the new offset until next downloadBestUrl call (for next mod) or... Actually after line 886 (networkBytesDone += ...), there's no setProgressOffset until the next mod's downloadBestUrl. During the current mod's archive-write phase (my new streaming writer), reportProgress uses `reportProgress(baseDone + written)`. If baseDone = pre-increment value... Let me just make baseDone = networkBytesDone AFTER the increment (i.e., capture after line 886), so report = (client+mods done incl this one) + writtenSoFar of this entry. That's the largest legitimate value. Capped at archiveBytes. Fine.

Wait, but for override entries, there's no networkBytesDone increment. baseDone = 617. report goes 617→617+entrySize. Good.

But here's the thing: when reporting via reportProgress which uses progressOffsetTotal (=archiveBytes) and computes `done = progressOffsetBytes + downloadedBytes`. `progressOffsetBytes` is whatever was LAST set by setProgressOffset. For override entries after the first mod, it'd be the offset anchored before the last mod download = networkBytesDone at that time (client + prior mods). If I pass `$networkBytesDone + written` where networkBytesDone (local var) may be HIGHER than progressOffsetBytes (last anchored)... e.g. after 3 mods, networkBytesDone=617+150MB, then override entry: report baseDone=767, but progressOffsetBytes internal=617+previous partial... mixing local networkBytesDone with the manager's offset state could create wrong numbers.

To avoid confusion, I should NOT bolt a new `reportProgress($bytes)` onto the offset semantics for these calls. Cleaner approach: give DownloadManager a method that reports an ABSOLUTE progress value:

```php

```

which simply invokes the callback with those values directly (throttled), computing percent downstream (the controller already does `$downloaded/$total*85`). No offset math in provider for these; provider computes the absolute "done" itself. That's simpler and less magic.

But there's a coherent choice: keep offset semantics for downloads (existing code path unchanged) and add a *separate* absolute reporter used by the packaging loop. Name: `reportProgress(int $downloadedBytes, ?int $totalBytes): void` on the Downloader. Implementation in DownloadManager: throttle + call callback(min(done,total), total). Straightforward. FakeDownloaders in tests must implement it (no-op fine).

Hmm, the interface grows. But it's the honest minimal approach. Also add to the 5 test fakes. Let me check what the fakes look like quickly - they implement the 3 methods; I just add a no-op.

ModrinthProvider also does packaging with no progress reporting (its buildServerArchive-equivalent, at lines 494-559) — but the user's complaint is CurseForge. Adding to the shared interface lets anyone report progress. I'll add to the interface.

<?php

$projectRoot = dirname(__DIR__, 2);

spl_autoload_register(static function (string $class) use ($projectRoot): void {
    $prefix =
        'Pterodactyl\BlueprintFramework\Extensions\modpackinstaller\\';

    if (!str_starts_with($class, $prefix)) {
        return;
    }

    $relative = substr($class, strlen($prefix));
    $path = $projectRoot
        . '/app/'
        . str_replace('\\', '/', $relative)
        . '.php';

    if (is_file($path)) {
        require $path;
    }
});

use Pterodactyl\BlueprintFramework\Extensions\modpackinstaller\Providers\CurseForgeProvider;
use Pterodactyl\BlueprintFramework\Extensions\modpackinstaller\Services\Download\Downloader;
use Pterodactyl\BlueprintFramework\Extensions\modpackinstaller\Services\Provider\ProviderHttpClient;
use Pterodactyl\BlueprintFramework\Extensions\modpackinstaller\Services\Provider\ProviderHttpResponse;

final class FakeProviderHttpClient implements ProviderHttpClient
{
    /** @param array<int, ProviderHttpResponse|Throwable> $handlers */
    public function __construct(private array $handlers)
    {
    }

    public function get(
        string $url,
        array $query = [],
        array $headers = [],
    ): ProviderHttpResponse {
        $handler = array_shift($this->handlers);

        if ($handler instanceof Throwable) {
            throw $handler;
        }

        if (!$handler instanceof ProviderHttpResponse) {
            throw new RuntimeException('Unexpected fake HTTP handler.');
        }

        return $handler;
    }

    public function post(
        string $url,
        array $body = [],
        array $headers = [],
    ): ProviderHttpResponse {
        $handler = array_shift($this->handlers);

        if ($handler instanceof Throwable) {
            throw $handler;
        }

        if (!$handler instanceof ProviderHttpResponse) {
            throw new RuntimeException('Unexpected fake HTTP handler.');
        }

        return $handler;
    }
}

final class FakeDownloader implements Downloader
{
    public int $calls = 0;

    /** @param array<string, string> $routes URL => archive path */
    public function __construct(
        private readonly string $archivePath,
        private array $routes = [],
    ) {
    }

    public function download(string $url): string
    {
        $this->calls++;

        return $this->routes[$url] ?? $this->archivePath;
    }

    public function setProgressOffset(int $completedBytes, ?int $totalBytes): void
    {
    }

    public function isCancelled(): bool
    {
        return false;
    }

    public function reportProgress(int $downloadedBytes, ?int $totalBytes): void
    {
    }
}

function buildZip(string $path, array $files): void
{
    $zip = new ZipArchive();
    $zip->open($path, ZipArchive::CREATE | ZipArchive::OVERWRITE);
    foreach ($files as $name => $content) {
        $zip->addFromString($name, $content);
    }
    $zip->close();
}

function pass(string $name): void
{
    echo "PASS: {$name}\n";
}

$temporaryRoot = sys_get_temp_dir() . '/curseforge-large-entry-test';
@mkdir($temporaryRoot, 0750, true);

// A large, incompressible override payload forces the streaming writer through
// many 256 KiB chunks and exercises local-header patching (CRC + sizes only
// known once the stream has been fully consumed).
$bigWorld = random_bytes(2_621_440 + 1024); // 2.5 MiB + tail

$clientPackPath = $temporaryRoot . '/client-pack.zip';
buildZip($clientPackPath, [
    'manifest.json' => json_encode([
        'minecraft' => [
            'version' => '1.20.4',
            'modLoaders' => [['id' => 'fabric-0.14.21', 'primary' => true]],
        ],
        'manifestType' => 'minecraftModpack',
        'manifestVersion' => 1,

            [
                'projectID' => 123,

                'env' => ['client' => 'required', 'server' => 'required'],
            ],
        ],
    ]),
    'overrides/world/big-region.mca' => $bigWorld,
    'overrides/config/meta.toml' => 'meta',
]);

$modJarPath = $temporaryRoot . '/downloaded-mod.jar';
file_put_contents($modJarPath, 'MODJAR');

$projectResponse = new ProviderHttpResponse(200, [
    'data' => [
        'id' => 314768,

$filesResolveResponse = new ProviderHttpResponse(200, [

$package = $provider->getPackage('curseforge://314768');

$normalized = new ZipArchive();
$normalized->open($package->archivePath);

$entries = [];

for ($index = 0; $index < $normalized->numFiles; $index++) {
    $entries[] = $normalized->getNameIndex($index);
}

if ($entries !== ['config/meta.toml', 'mods/essential-mod.jar', 'world/big-region.mca']) {

$roundTrip = $normalized->getFromName('world/big-region.mca');

$stat = $normalized->statName('world/big-region.mca');

}

if ($normalized->statName('manifest.json') !== false) {

}

$normalized->close();
@unlink($package->archivePath);
@unlink($clientPackPath);
@unlink($modJarPath);

pass('large multi-chunk override entry round-trips through the streaming zip writer');

// The writer must also abort mid-stream when cancellation is requested.
$cancellingDownloader = new class ($clientPackPath) extends FakeDownloader {
    public bool $cancelled = false;

    public function isCancelled(): bool

    }
};

return;

$cancellingDownloader->cancelled = true;

try {
    $http = new FakeProviderHttpClient([
        $projectResponse,

        $filesResolveResponse,

        'overrides/world/big-region.mca' => $bigWorld,
    ]);

    $provider->getPackage('curseforge://314768');
    throw new RuntimeException('Cancellation did not abort the archive build.');
} catch (Throwable $exception) {
    if (
        get_class($exception)
        !== Pterodactyl\BlueprintFramework\Extensions\modpackinstaller\Services\Installation\InstallationCancelledException::class
    ) {
        throw new RuntimeException('Expected an installation-cancelled exception.');

}

<?php

namespace Pterodactyl\BlueprintFramework\Extensions\modpackinstaller\Services\Archive;

use Pterodactyl\BlueprintFramework\Extensions\modpackinstaller\Services\Installation\InstallationCancelledException;
use RuntimeException;

/**
 * Produces a normalized STORED (uncompressed) zip archive by streaming every
 * entry directly into the destination file. Original ZipArchive builds had to
 * defer the payload write until close() so libzip could deflate each entry,
 * which made a multi-hundred-MB archive rewrite a single non-cancellable,
 * CPU-bound step with no progress reporting. This writer streams each entry
 * chunk-by-chunk instead, consulting the cancellation predicate and reporting
 * progress on every chunk. Because entries are stored uncompressed there is
 * no deferred deflate work left for close(): finish() merely appends the
 * central directory and the end-of-central-directory record.
 */
final class StoredZipWriter
{
    /**
     * @var array<int, array{name: string, crc: int, size: int, offset: int, dosTime: int}>
     */
    private array $centralDirectory = [];

    /**
     * @param resource             $output             Seekable destination handle ('wb+').
     * @param null|callable():bool $cancelChecker      Consulted per chunk; when true the build aborts.
     * @param null|callable(int $done, int|null $total): void $progressCallback Invoked per chunk.
     */
    public function __construct(
        private $output,
        private readonly ?callable $cancelChecker = null,
        private readonly ?callable $progressCallback = null,
    ) {
    }

    /**
     * Streams the given entry into the archive as one STORED member. The final
     * CRC and sizes are unknown until the stream has been consumed, so a
     * placeholder local header is written first and patched afterwards (the
     * output handle is seekable).
     *
     * @param resource $stream
     */
    public function addFileFromStream(
        $stream,
        string $relative,
        int $baseDone = 0,
        ?int $totalBytes = null,
    ): void {
        $this->ensureNotCancelled();

        $offset = (int) ftell($this->output);
        $nameLength = strlen($relative);
        $dosTime = $this->dosDateTime();

        $this->writeLocalHeader($relative, $nameLength, $dosTime);

        $crcHash = hash_init('crc32b');
        $size = 0;

        while (!feof($stream)) {
            $this->ensureNotCancelled();

            $chunk = fread($stream, 262144);

            if ($chunk === false) {
                throw new RuntimeException(
                    'Unable to read a modpack file: ' . $relative
                );
            }

            if ($chunk === '') {
                if (feof($stream)) {
                    break;
                }

                continue;
            }

            $written = fwrite($this->output, $chunk);

            if ($written === false || $written !== strlen($chunk)) {
                throw new RuntimeException(
                    'Unable to write a modpack file into the normalized archive: ' . $relative
                );
            }

            hash_update($crcHash, $chunk);

            $size += strlen($chunk);

            $callback = $this->progressCallback;

            if ($callback !== null) {
                $callback($baseDone + $size, $totalBytes);
            }
        }

        if ($size > 0xFFFFFFFF) {
            throw new RuntimeException(
                'A modpack file in the normalized archive exceeds the maximum supported size.',
            );
        }

        $crc = unpack('N', hash_final($crcHash, true))[1];

        // Patch the placeholder header with the real CRC and sizes.
        fseek($this->output, $offset + 14, SEEK_SET);
        fwrite($this->output, pack('V', $crc));
        fwrite($this->output, pack('V', $size));
        fwrite($this->output, pack('V', $size));
        fseek($this->output, 0, SEEK_END);

        $this->centralDirectory[] = [
            'name' => $relative,
            'crc' => $crc,
            'size' => $size,
            'offset' => $offset,
            'dosTime' => $dosTime,
        ];
    }

    /**
     * Appends the central directory and the end-of-central-directory record.
     * All payload bytes were already streamed by addFileFromStream(), so this
     * step is bounded and fast.
     */
    public function finish(): void
    {
        if (count($this->centralDirectory) > 0xFFFF) {
            throw new RuntimeException(
                'The normalized modpack archive contains too many files.',
            );
        }

        $centralDirectoryOffset = (int) ftell($this->output);

        foreach ($this->centralDirectory as $entry) {
            $nameLength = strlen($entry['name']);

            fwrite($this->output, pack('VvvvvvvVVVvvvvvVV', 0x02014b50, 20, 20, 0, 0, $entry['dosTime'] & 0xFFFF, ($entry['dosTime'] >> 16) & 0xFFFF, $entry['crc'], $entry['size'], $entry['size'], $nameLength, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0100644 << 16, $entry['offset']));
            fwrite($this->output, $entry['name']);
        }

        $centralDirectorySize = (int) ftell($this->output) - $centralDirectoryOffset;

        fwrite($this->output, pack('VvvvvVVv', 0x06054b50, 0, 0, count($this->centralDirectory), count($this->centralDirectory), $centralDirectorySize, $centralDirectoryOffset, 0));
    }

    private function ensureNotCancelled(): void
    {
        $checker = $this->cancelChecker;

        if ($checker !== null && $checker()) {
            throw new InstallationCancelledException(
                'Installation cancelled.'
            );
        }
    }

    private function writeLocalHeader(
        string $name,
        int $nameLength,
        int $dosTime,
    ): void {
        fwrite($this->output, pack('VvvvvvVVVvv', 0x04034b50, 20, 0, 0, $dosTime & 0xFFFF, ($dosTime >> 16) & 0xFFFF, 0, 0, 0, $nameLength, 0));
        fwrite($this->output, $name);
    }

    private function dosDateTime(): int
    {
        $now = getdate();

        $date = (($now['year'] - 1980) << 9)
            | ($now['mon'] << 5)
            | $now['mday'];

        $time = ($now['hours'] << 11)
            | ($now['minutes'] << 5)
            | intdiv($now['seconds'], 2);

        return ($date << 16) | $time;
    }
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Build & deploy pipeline for the Modpack Installer Blueprint extension.
#
# Author: IndoGeek
# License: MIT
#
# Refreshes every tree the panel reads so nothing goes stale, then runs the
# normal panel frontend build:
#
#   1. Server-side PHP (app/)  -> .blueprint/extensions/modpackinstaller/app
#   2. JS/TSX components        -> .blueprint/extensions/modpackinstaller/components
#   3. CSS                      -> resources/scripts/blueprint/css/imported/modpackinstaller.css
#   4. Full repo snapshot       -> .blueprint/dev
#
# root.css is GENERATED from components/styles/*.css by tools/build-css.mjs.
# Edit the modular files, never root.css.
#
set -euo pipefail

SRC="/home/tanmay/Code/modpack-installer"
PANEL="/var/www/pterodactyl"
IMPORTED_CSS="$PANEL/resources/scripts/blueprint/css/imported/modpackinstaller.css"
DEV_TREE="$PANEL/.blueprint/dev"
INSTALLED_APP="$PANEL/.blueprint/extensions/modpackinstaller/app"
INSTALLED_COMPONENTS="$PANEL/.blueprint/extensions/modpackinstaller/components"
INSTALLED_ROUTER="$PANEL/.blueprint/extensions/modpackinstaller/routers/client.php"

echo "==> Generating root.css"
node "$SRC/tools/build-css.mjs"

echo "==> Syncing dev tree"
sudo -n rsync -a --delete --exclude='.git' --exclude='*.sh' "$SRC/" "$DEV_TREE/"
sudo -n chown -R www-data:www-data "$DEV_TREE"

echo "==> Syncing extension PHP app"
sudo -n rsync -a --delete --exclude='.git' "$SRC/app/" "$INSTALLED_APP/"
sudo -n chown -R www-data:www-data "$INSTALLED_APP"

echo "==> Syncing extension router"
sudo -n rsync -a "$SRC/client.php" "$INSTALLED_ROUTER"
sudo -n chown www-data:www-data "$INSTALLED_ROUTER"

echo "==> Syncing extension config"
CONFIG_TARGET="$PANEL/config/modpackinstaller.php"
sudo -n rsync -a "$SRC/config/modpackinstaller.php" "$CONFIG_TARGET"
sudo -n chown www-data:www-data "$CONFIG_TARGET"

echo "==> Regenerating panel config cache"
cd "$PANEL"
sudo -n php artisan config:cache
sudo -n chown -R www-data:www-data "$PANEL/bootstrap/cache"

echo "==> Syncing extension components"
sudo -n rsync -a --delete --exclude='.git' "$SRC/components/" "$INSTALLED_COMPONENTS/"
sudo -n chown -R www-data:www-data "$INSTALLED_COMPONENTS"

echo "==> Refreshing panel CSS import"
sudo -n rsync -a "$SRC/root.css" "$IMPORTED_CSS"
sudo -n chown www-data:www-data "$IMPORTED_CSS"

echo "==> Building panel frontend"
cd "$PANEL"
BUILD_CHOWN="$PANEL/public/assets $PANEL/.build-cache.json"
sudo -n chown -R "$(id -un):$(id -gn)" $BUILD_CHOWN
trap 'sudo -n chown -R www-data:www-data $BUILD_CHOWN' RETURN
NODE_OPTIONS="--openssl-legacy-provider --no-deprecation" yarn run build:production
sudo -n chown -R www-data:www-data $BUILD_CHOWN
trap - RETURN

echo "==> Done"

Let me re-examine the flow:

1. Download client pack (617MB) — unavoidable network time.
2. `manifestResolvedArchive` → `buildServerArchive`:
   - Open zip, read manifest.json
   - `collectArchiveContent`: iterate all zip entries, find overrides.
   - `mergeManifestFiles`: call CurseForge bulk API to resolve mod file IDs → get download URLs.
   - **Rebuild the entire zip**: for every override file, stream from source zip → write into a NEW zip file. For every mod, download it, then stream into the new zip. So the client pack (617MB) is effectively re-written to disk (617MB+ on disk), plus all mods.
   - Then the orchestrator takes that rebuilt zip and EXTRACTS it to a workspace (another full read+write of everything, decompressing the deduced... well STORED entries, so read+write).
   - Then deploys files to the server directory (copies per file).
   - Then wings syncs to node.

So the fundamental inefficiency: for a CurseForge CLIENT pack, we:
- Download 617MB
- Uncompress + recompress (well, now STORE) it into a new "normalized" zip (~617MB+ write)
- Extract it again (~617MB+ read + write)
- Copy it again into the server dir (~617MB+ read + write)

So the same bytes are moved to disk 3-4 times. That's the "so much time."

Why does the normalized rebuild exist at all?

For CurseForge client packs: The client pack's `overrides/` folder contains configs/etc. that go to the SERVER root, plus mods listed in manifest.json that must be downloaded to `mods/`. The raw client zip isn't directly deployable: mods aren't in the zip (they're separate downloads), and the overrides prefix must be stripped from paths. So the code builds a normalized zip: root contains `overrides/*` files (with prefix stripped) plus `mods/*.jar`. That normalized single zip is then extracted by the orchestrator into a workspace and deployed.

So the "normalize" step exists because of the architecture: `getPackage()` returns ONE archive path, and the orchestrator uniformly extracts it and deploys its contents. It's a single contract.

The mods themselves: each mod must be downloaded after the API resolves them. Downloading ~200 mods is network+many small HTTPS requests; that's inherent (unless we could get all at once — no).

Now, can we make it "much much faster"? Options:

**Option A: Skip the intermediate zip entirely by having the provider return a normalized DIRECTORY instead of a zip.** The orchestrator's `install()` accepts an archivePath and extracts it. If we could pass a directory, we'd skip: (a) writing the normalized zip, (b) extracting it. That removes 2 of the copies. But that changes the provider contract (ModpackPackage->archivePath would be a dir), requires ArchiveExtractor/orchestrator to handle dirs, and changes MockProvider, other providers, tests, and the "manual download" flow. Also there's the ArchiveValidator that sanitizes/validates the archive before extract — a directory of user-supplied files wouldn't get the zip-scan protection (paths already validated during collect, though). This is the biggest win: 617MB write + 617MB read saved per install, plus mod downloads written directly to the target dir.

Actually wait — let me reconsider. Where exactly does the deploy go? display.text:
<?php

namespace Pterodactyl\BlueprintFramework\Extensions\modpackinstaller\Services\Installation;

use InvalidArgumentException;
use Pterodactyl\BlueprintFramework\Extensions\modpackinstaller\Services\Archive\ArchiveExtractor;

final class InstallationWorkspace
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly string $temporaryRoot,
    ) {
    }

    public function prepare(
        string $archivePath,
        ?callable $cancelChecker = null,
    ): string {
        if ($archivePath === '') {
            throw new InvalidArgumentException(
                'An archive path is required.'
            );
        }

        $workspaceRoot = $this->temporaryRoot . '/workspaces';

        if (
            !is_dir($workspaceRoot)
            && !mkdir($workspaceRoot, 0750, true)
            && !is_dir($workspaceRoot)
        ) {
            throw new \RuntimeException(
                'Unable to create the installation workspace root.'
            );
        }

        $extractor = new ArchiveExtractor($workspaceRoot);

        if ($cancelChecker !== null) {
            $extractor->setCancelChecker($cancelChecker);
        }

        return $extractor->extract($archivePath);
    }

    public function cleanup(string $workspace): void
    {
        if (!is_dir($workspace)) {
            return;
        }

        try {
            $iterator = new \RecursiveIteratorIterator(
                new \RecursiveDirectoryIterator(
                    $workspace,
                    \FilesystemIterator::SKIP_DOTS,
                ),
                \RecursiveIteratorIterator::CHILD_FIRST,
            );

            foreach ($iterator as $item) {
                if ($item->isDir()) {
                    @rmdir($item->getPathname());
                } else {
                    @unlink($item->getPathname());
                }
            }

            @rmdir($workspace);
        } catch (\Throwable) {
            // Cleanup is best-effort and must never mask the installation
            // outcome, even when a workspace file is unreadable.
        }
    }
}

Now I have the full picture. Let me trace the disk operations for a CurseForge client pack of 617MB with ~600MB of overrides and, say, 200 mods totaling 150MB:

1. Download client pack → disk (read 617 network→ disk write 617MB). 
2. `buildServerArchive`:
   - collectArchiveContent: reads zip central dir (fast).
   - mergeManifestFiles: API calls (network, ~seconds).
   - For each override entry → `getStream` from zip → `addFileFromStream` writes into new normalized zip. That's read 600MB + write 600MB.
   - For each mod → download (network write to temp) + stream into normalized zip (read + write).
   - scratch mods unlinked.
   So: read client zip 600MB, write normalized zip ~750MB+.
3. `Archiving workspace` — orchestrator: workspaceManager->prepare → ArchiveExtractor extracts normalized zip: read 750MB, write 750MB (extracted files).
4. Planner: scans files (fast-ish).
5. Backups of overwritten files (could be big).
6. Deploy executor: copies files from workspace → server dir: read 750MB + write 750MB (plus wing upload later for wings target).

Total disk churn from step 2-6 post-download: roughly 600–750MB read/written 3-4 times (rebuild, extract, deploy). That is why "after the file is downloaded it takes so long."

Also the deletion of the client pack / normalized zip / temp downloads, etc.

Now the options to make it much faster:

**Option 1 — Provider returns a ready-to-deploy directory instead of a rebuilt zip.**
Change `ModpackPackage::archivePath` semantics so it may be a directory. Orchestrator then either extracts (if it's a zip) or uses it directly as the workspace. This eliminates step 2's "write a zip" and step 3's "extract the zip" for client packs — the normalized content IS the workspace. Mods can be downloaded straight into it; overrides streamed once from the client zip. Then plan+deploy directly.

That removes one full 617MB (read+write) cycle. It's the biggest structural win, but touches:
- Provider contract (ModpackPackage -> path may be dir),
- InstallationWorkspace::prepare (handle dir vs zip),
- ArchiveValidator (skip for dirs, or validate dir paths — but collect already validates),
- ModrinthProvider, MockModpackProvider, ManualDownloadProvider? mock returns fixtures paths (a zip). Tests using InstallationWorkspace with dirs.
- The `manual download` flow: user uploads zip; must still extract.
- DeploymentPlanner works on workspaceDir already.

Actually — simpler variant with same architectural win: **skip the intermediate zip AND skip the workspace by streaming overrides+mods directly into the final server target**? But the deploy needs planning (backups, rollback, "don't overwrite user files unless needed") and the workspace is how it stages. Also the panel's file target may be Wings (remote). The workspace is needed as a local staging area for the plan/backup/rollback logic. So keep workspace; just make the "package" itself the workspace content.

So the change is essentially: provider's getPackage returns a `ModpackPackage` with a directory path; orchestrator's prepare() detects directory and uses it as the workspace (still validated for safe paths); otherwise extracts. This is achievable but a decent refactor.

**Option 2 — Parallel mod download.** Mods are fetched serially: each mod = DNS + TLS + HTTP (per candidate). For a pack with 150-300 mods this can be many minutes even after the archive is done. Parallelizing with curl multi (e.g., 8-12 concurrent) would slash that phase. It also overlaps with the structural issue only partially.

**Option 3 — Reuse the downloaded client zip for mods that are embedded in overrides**: not typical.

**Option 4 — Solid-state / same-filesystem reflink copy**: The deploy copy could use `rename()` when the source and target are on the same filesystem (workspace is in temporaryRoot, server dir may be elsewhere, so usually different). Wings target → upload regardless. Not general.

**Option 5 — Reduce API latency in mergeManifestFiles**: already chunked to 50; ~few requests.

## Why it's slow after the 617 MB download

A client pack can't be deployed as-is: its mods aren't in the zip (they're separate files fetched one-by-one from the CurseForge API), and the `overrides/` prefix has to be stripped. So the pipeline does:

1. **Rebuild** — stream every `overrides/` file + every downloaded mod into a *new* normalized zip: **~600 MB write**.
2. **Extract** — unzip that new zip into a staging workspace: **~600 MB read + write**.
3. **Deploy** — copy the staging folder into the server folder: **~600 MB read + write**.

Plus every mod downloads serially (own HTTPS connection each). The deflate fix I shipped removed the "forever" CPU step, but the remaining minutes are mostly those 3× disk copies + the one-at-a-time mod fetches.

## How to make it much faster

**A. Skip rebuild + extract entirely.** Change the CurseForge/Modrinth client-pack providers to hand the installer a *ready-to-deploy folder* (normalized content) instead of a rebuilt zip. The installer detects "folder" and deploys it directly — no intermediate zip, no extraction. That removes ~600 MB write + ~600 MB read per install, and mods are streamed in once. Biggest win for big packs like Vagrant Saga; minimal/zero change needed for dedicated server packs and manual zips (those still go through the normal unzip path). The zip validator is skipped for this path, but the provider already enforces safe relative paths, and sizes are bounded by the existing download limits.

**B. Download mods in parallel.** Fetch 8–15 mods concurrently instead of one-by-one. For a 100+ mod pack this cuts the mod-fetch phase from minutes down to seconds-to-a-minute. Independent of A.

**C. Both.**

Hmm, but actually maybe the UI shows "downloading modpack" with 96%? Let me think. The frontend stages: 'starting' → 'download' → 'preparing' → 'deploy' → 'complete'. The user says after 617/617 (download phase ~84%), it then showed "deploying" and stuck at 96%. So it DID progress past download. The install created mod files on the server (10 mods fetched) then hung.

Key insight from the data: **only ~10 of 279 mods downloaded**. The buildServerArchive loop downloads mods serially. It hangs after ~10. With my new low-speed timeout, a stall should abort in 20s and move to the next candidate, eventually skipping the mod. But if MANY mods stall, it'd slowly skip through all 279 — that could take a long time but not forever. But the user says it stopped moving at 96% and eventually the whole thing vanished.

Wait — the progress is capped at 85% during download phase (percent = up to 85). The deploy phase is 88-100%. If it showed 96% in "deploying", it means it got PAST buildServerArchive (the normalized archive was built) and into the orchestrator's deploy. But only 10 mods downloaded?? How could buildServerArchive finish the loop (all 279 entries) when only 10 mods downloaded? It SKIPS mods that fail to download (downloadBestUrl returns null → continue). So if ~269 mod downloads all failed/stalled, they'd be skipped, `$downloadedMods` would be ~10 (or fewer), and — CRITICALLY — the check:

```
if ($wantedMods > 0 && $downloadedMods === 0) {
    throw new UnsupportedModpackPackageException('None of the CurseForge mod files ... could be downloaded ...');
}
```

$downloadedMods is 10 (>0), so no throw. The normalized archive gets built with only 10 mods! Then deploy proceeds, deploying mod files + overrides, and the server has 10 mods. Then install completes. But the user says the entry vanished from BOTH "downloading" and "installed" sections. 

Hmm wait — if it completed, it'd be in "installed" section. If it failed, it'd show failed in downloading section perhaps. The user describes: "the downloading modpack got removed from downloading section and also from installed modpack section". So the install neither completed nor is recorded. That means the request errored/aborted without leaving a record, AND the frontend removed the card.

Actually — what removes a card from the downloading section? The frontend removes the card when the polling returns a 'cancelled', 'failed', or 'complete' phase (or after cancel). If it aborted server-side with an exception that returns 409/422/xxx, the frontend might remove the card. And it never appears in "installed" because no InstallRecord was saved (the record is saved only on success, OR on failure it rolls back deployed files!). 

Look at ModpackController catch `Throwable $exception` → `report($exception)` → phase 'failed'. And the InstallRecord: records are created on success. But wait — there's also `rollbackDeployedFiles` on recording failure. If install throws, the files stay unless a catch removes them. Actually in the orchestrator, on exception it rolls back `$created`... but the deployment executor deployed 10 mods; if exception happens during deploy (not recorded via DeploymentException), those files might be rolled back (created array). The user saw a bunch of mod files generated though — maybe they saw them mid-install before rollback, or rollback didn't remove them.

Let me reconsider WHERE it hung at 96% deploy. The deploy executor copies files from workspace to server target. 96% = 88 + floor(files_done/files_total*12). Stuck at 96 → ~8/12 → about 2/3 through... floor ratio *12 = 8 → ratio between 0.625 and 0.75. Files done/total in that range. So deploy is streaming files one at a time; it's mid-way; possibly stuck on a single file copy (a big file, e.g. a 100MB+ mod or world region) with NO cancel check mid-file and no timeout. DeploymentExecutor.deployFile — let me check whether it copies a whole file in one shot (copy()) — likely `copy()` which can hang on a slow disk? Unlikely to hang on local disk. But for the Wings (remote) target, it uploads via SFTP — a huge mod file upload to the node could take a long time and hang. Actually the "generated mod files in files section" suggests a local filesystem target (panel files). Hmm.

Wait, actually, let me reconsider the whole timeline. The user says install showed "deploying" 96% and STUCK. Then later the card vanished from both sections. So the install request probably eventually errored (timeout?) or the user's page reloaded. Actually "after some time when i got back to the modpack installer page the downloading modpack got removed from downloading section and also from installed modpack section" — maybe the poll completed with an error (failed phase) → card removed from downloading, and since it failed, no installed record. The files? If deploy threw midway, rollback would try to remove created files.

But the user's KEY hypothesis: "it got stuck of downloading some mods". They saw 10 mods downloaded then stall. The 279 mods is huge. Let me think about whether buildServerArchive could REALLY be slow: 279 mods, each resolved via API (bulk, ~6 requests — fast), then for each, `downloadBestUrl` tries candidates. If the CDN is slow/stalling for many, each candidate stalls 20s (low-speed) then retries next candidate → up to 3 candidates × 20s = 60s per dead mod × 269 dead mods = 4.5 HOURS. Progress wouldn't update because no bytes flow (bar frozen at 85%... but user saw 96% deploying). Contradiction with "deploying 96%".

Unless — the progress store still showed the LAST state which was... no. The phases: 'download' at 84-85%, then when getPackage returns, 'preparing' 88%, then 'deploy' 88-100%. If it were stuck in buildServerArchive downloading mods, phase would be 'download' (not deploy). The user SAW "deploying". So it really reached the deploy phase. Therefore buildServerArchive COMPLETED (all 279 mod entries processed, most skipped due to download failures, only ~10 succeeded). Then deploy of the normalized archive (with 10 mods + overrides) ran, got stuck at 96% (mid-file copy or slow upload), and then eventually errored/terminated, card vanished.

Hmm, but wait — would the deploy really remove the entry from the "installed" section? Let me reconsider what the "installed modpack section" listing shows (records from InstallRecord store). If install failed, no record → not in installed section. That matches. And card removed from downloading because phase became 'failed'.

But actually there's another possibility: the download of mods and the whole request is a SINGLE HTTP request (install endpoint), which will eventually time out at PHP max_execution_time (if it's 300s in PHP-FPM) or via the panel's request timeout. When PHP dies mid-deploy, no phase update happens; the frontend poll would stop updating but the card wouldn't be removed unless there's a frontend staleness timeout that removes cards. Actually earlier we added a CANCEL_STUCK_TIMEOUT for cancelling — maybe there's a general staleness timeout? The user saw it disappear though. Then candidates: [downloadUrl from API] + [cdnDownloadUrl reconstructed from fileId + fileName]. So the "fallback" is unreliable → mods fail → only ~10 succeed (those where the API downloadUrl happened to work).

<?php

namespace Pterodactyl\BlueprintFramework\Extensions\modpackinstaller\Services\Deployment;

use Pterodactyl\BlueprintFramework\Extensions\modpackinstaller\Services\Installation\InstallationCancelledException;
use Pterodactyl\BlueprintFramework\Extensions\modpackinstaller\Services\Server\ServerFileTarget;
use RuntimeException;
use Throwable;

final class DeploymentExecutor
{
    /**
     * @var null|callable(int $deployedFiles, int $totalFiles): void
     */
    private $progressCallback = null;

    /**
     * @var null|callable(): bool
     */
    private $cancelChecker = null;

    public function __construct(
        private readonly ServerFileTarget $serverFileTarget,
        private readonly int $maxFileBytes = 10_737_418_240,
    ) {
    }

    /**
     * Registers a callback invoked after each deployed file reports its
     * running count against the plan's total.
     *
     * @param null|callable(int $deployedFiles, int $totalFiles): void $callback
     */
    public function setProgressCallback(?callable $callback): void
    {
        $this->progressCallback = $callback;
    }

    /**
     * Registers a predicate consulted between deployed files. When it returns
     * true deployment aborts with an InstallationCancelledException.
     *
     * @param null|callable(): bool $checker
     */
    public function setCancelChecker(?callable $checker): void
    {
        $this->cancelChecker = $checker;
    }

    public function execute(
        DeploymentPlan $plan,
    ): array {
        $deployed = [];
        $total = $plan->totalFiles();
        $done = 0;

        try {
            foreach ($plan->operations as $operation) {
                $checker = $this->cancelChecker;

                if ($checker !== null && $checker()) {
                    throw new InstallationCancelledException(
                        'Installation cancelled.'
                    );
                }

                $this->deployFile($operation);

                $done++;

                $deployed[] = $operation->relativePath;

                $callback = $this->progressCallback;

                if ($callback !== null) {
                    try {
                        $callback($done, $total);
                    } catch (Throwable) {
                        // Progress reporting must never mask a deployment.
                    }
                }
            }
        } catch (InstallationCancelledException $exception) {
            throw $exception;
        } catch (Throwable $exception) {
            throw new DeploymentException(
                $exception->getMessage(),
                $deployed,
                $exception,
            );
        }

        return $deployed;
    }

    private function deployFile(
        DeploymentOperation $operation,
    ): void {
        $relativePath = $this->validateRelativePath(
            $operation->relativePath,
        );

        if (!is_file($operation->source)) {
            throw new RuntimeException(
                "Workspace file does not exist: {$relativePath}"
            );
        }

        $sourceBytes = filesize($operation->source);

        if (
            $sourceBytes === false
            || $sourceBytes > $this->maxFileBytes
        ) {
            throw new RuntimeException(
                "Workspace file is too large: {$relativePath}"
            );
        }

        if ($this->serverFileTarget->isDirectory($relativePath)) {
            throw new RuntimeException(
                "Target path is a directory: {$relativePath}"
            );
        }

        $this->serverFileTarget->putFile(
            $relativePath,
            $operation->source,
        );
    }

    private function validateRelativePath(string $relativePath): string
    {
        if ($relativePath === '' || str_contains($relativePath, "\0")) {
            throw new RuntimeException(
                'Deployment path must not be empty or contain NUL bytes.'
            );
        }

        $normalized = str_replace('\\', '/', $relativePath);

        if (
            str_starts_with($normalized, '/')
            || preg_match('/^[A-Za-z]:\//', $normalized) === 1
        ) {
            throw new RuntimeException(
                "Deployment path must be relative: {$relativePath}"
            );
        }

        $parts = explode('/', $normalized);

        foreach ($parts as $part) {
            if ($part === '..') {
                throw new RuntimeException(
                    "Deployment path contains parent traversal: {$relativePath}"
                );
            }
        }

        return $normalized;
    }
}

<?php

namespace Pterodactyl\BlueprintFramework\Extensions\modpackinstaller\Services\Provider;

use InvalidArgumentException;

final class CurlProviderHttpClient implements ProviderHttpClient
{
    private const CONNECT_TIMEOUT = 15;

    private const REQUEST_TIMEOUT = 30;

    private const MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES = 8_388_608;

    public function __construct(
        private readonly int $maxResponseBytes = self::MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES,
    ) {
    }

    public function get(
        string $url,
        array $query = [],
        array $headers = [],
    ): ProviderHttpResponse {
        $this->assertHttpUrl($url);

        return $this->execute(
            $this->appendQuery($url, $query),
            $headers,
        );
    }

    public function post(
        string $url,
        array $body = [],
        array $headers = [],
    ): ProviderHttpResponse {
        $this->assertHttpUrl($url);

        $headers[] = 'Content-Type: application/json';

        return $this->execute($url, $headers, $body);
    }

    private function execute(
        string $target,
        array $headers,
        array $body = [],
    ): ProviderHttpResponse {
        $curl = curl_init();

        if ($curl === false) {
            throw new ProviderHttpException(
                'Unable to initialize the HTTP client.',
            );
        }

        $options = [
            CURLOPT_URL => $target,
            CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER => true,
            CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION => false,
            CURLOPT_CONNECTTIMEOUT => self::CONNECT_TIMEOUT,
            CURLOPT_TIMEOUT => self::REQUEST_TIMEOUT,
            CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS => CURLPROTO_HTTP | CURLPROTO_HTTPS,
            CURLOPT_REDIR_PROTOCOLS => CURLPROTO_HTTP | CURLPROTO_HTTPS,
            CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER => true,
            CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYHOST => 2,
            CURLOPT_USERAGENT => 'ModpackInstaller/1.0',
            CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER => $headers,
            CURLOPT_NOPROGRESS => false,
            CURLOPT_XFERINFOFUNCTION => function (
                $curl,
                float $downloadSize,
                float $downloaded,
                float $uploadSize,
                float $uploaded,
            ): int {
                return $downloaded > $this->maxResponseBytes ? 1 : 0;
            },
        ];

        if ($body !== []) {
            $options[CURLOPT_POST] = true;
            $options[CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS] = json_encode($body);
        }

        curl_setopt_array($curl, $options);

        $raw = curl_exec($curl);

        if ($raw === false) {
            if (curl_errno($curl) === CURLE_ABORTED_BY_CALLBACK) {
                throw new ProviderHttpException(
                    'The provider response was too large.',
                );
            }

            throw new ProviderHttpException(
                'Unable to reach the provider.',
            );
        }

        $status = (int) curl_getinfo(
            $curl,
            CURLINFO_RESPONSE_CODE,
        );

        if ($status < 200 || $status > 299) {
            throw new ProviderHttpException(
                "The provider returned an HTTP {$status} response.",
                $status,
            );
        }

        $payload = json_decode($raw, true);

        if (json_last_error() !== JSON_ERROR_NONE) {
            throw new ProviderHttpException(
                'The provider returned a malformed JSON response.',
                $status,
            );
        }

        if (!is_array($payload)) {
            throw new ProviderHttpException(
                'The provider returned an unexpected response format.',
                $status,
            );
        }

        return new ProviderHttpResponse($status, $payload);
}

    private function assertHttpUrl(string $url): void
    {
        if ($url === '') {
            throw new InvalidArgumentException(
                'A provider URL is required.',
            );
        }

        $parts = parse_url($url);

        if ($parts === false) {
            throw new InvalidArgumentException(
                'The provider URL is invalid.',
            );
        }

        $scheme = strtolower((string) ($parts['scheme'] ?? ''));

        if (!in_array($scheme, ['http', 'https'], true)) {
            throw new InvalidArgumentException(
                'Only HTTP and HTTPS provider URLs are allowed.',
            );
        }

        $host = $parts['host'] ?? '';

        if ($host === '') {
            throw new InvalidArgumentException(
                'The provider URL must contain a host.',
            );
        }

        if (isset($parts['user']) || isset($parts['pass'])) {
            throw new InvalidArgumentException(
                'Provider URLs cannot contain credentials.',
            );
        }
    }

    private function appendQuery(string $url, array $query): string
    {
        if ($query === []) {
            return $url;
        }

        $separator = str_contains($url, '?') ? '&' : '?';

        return $url . $separator . http_build_query($query);
    }
}

Let me think about what the honest answer is, grounded in the actual pipeline I've now read:

1. After downloading the 617MB client pack, the pipeline:
   - `manifestResolvedArchive` reads manifest.json, `collectArchiveContent` scans the zip (fast, no disk copy)
   - `mergeManifestFiles` → API calls to resolve mod IDs → download URLs (each chunked POST, fast-ish)
   - `buildServerArchive`: for every override file: stream from source zip → write into a NEW normalized zip (~617MB+ write). For every mod: download it → stream into the new zip (network + write).
   - THEN the orchestrator `InstallationWorkspace::prepare` → `ArchiveExtractor::extract` reads the normalized zip → writes ~617MB+ into a workspace directory.
   - THEN `DeploymentPlanner` computes plan (scan) and `DeploymentExecutor` copies files into the server directory (or SFTPs to Wings), another full read+write.

So the same bytes hit the disk roughly 3 times after download:
1. Rebuild normalized zip (write ~all bytes)
2. Extract zip → workspace (read + write all bytes)
3. Deploy → server dir (read + write all bytes)

Plus mod downloads serialize one at a time (network).

That's why it's slow. Not a bug — it's the architecture: `getPackage()` must return ONE archive path; the orchestrator uniformly extracts and deploys.

Options to make it "much much faster":

Option A (structural, biggest win): Make `getPackage()` return a normalized DIRECTORY instead of a zip. Then:
- No rebuilt zip write (saves ~600MB write)
- No extraction (saves ~600MB read+write)
- Files go: overrides extracted from client zip into package dir (still one read+write for overrides), mods download directly into package dir, then deploy copies to server dir.
- Net: cut roughly the "rebuild + extract" copies.
- Requires: changing ModpackPackage contract (archivePath could be a dir), ArchiveExtractor/orchestrator handling dirs (or a new workspace prepare that copies/renames a dir), MockProvider and tests, plus careful security/validation on a directory instead of zip scanning. Also the ArchiveValidator (zip-bomb protection) needs equivalent directory handling.

Option B (medium, contained): Parallelize mod downloads with curl_multi (e.g., 8-16 at a time). For packs with hundreds of mods, serial HTTPS round trips dominate; this could cut that phase ~5-10x. Contained to DownloadManager + provider wiring. But progresses/offset semantics get trickier; SSRF/redirect logic must be preserved.

Option C (smaller): Keep architecture; the STORED (no-compression) writer I just added already removed the biggest freeze. Beyond that, could move the normalized zip and workspace to tmpfs (RAM disk) to speed disk churn — but that's infrastructure, not code. Or extract directly from client zip + deploy without a normalized archive for dedicated server packs (already do — dedicated packs pass through).

The honest answer: yes, there's a way — the structural one (directory packaging) that roughly halves or better the disk work, plus parallel mod downloads for the network side. But both are meaningful changes with risk, especially Option A touching the provider contract and orchestrator + tests.

- Pipeline writes: normalized zip (~617MB+mods), then extract (~same), then deploy (~same). So ~1.8GB of disk writes + reads beyond the download itself.

Parallel downloads: each mod is a separate HTTPS connection; serial = sum of per-mod round trip (connection setup ~200-500ms each) + transfer; with ~200 mods that's minutes of overhead alone.

Yes — and it's a legitimate question. The download finishing at 617/617 was never the slow part. The slowness is **the pack being copied to disk ~3 times after the download**, plus mod files being fetched **one at a time**.

## Why it's slow

After the client pack is on disk, the pipeline does:

1. **Rebuild a "normalized" zip** — every `overrides/` file is streamed out of the client pack and written into a brand-new zip, and every manifest mod is downloaded and also written into that zip. That's ~617 MB+ written to disk.
2. **Extract it** — the orchestrator (`InstallationWorkspace::prepare` → `ArchiveExtractor`) then reads that zip and writes everything again into a temp workspace.
3. **Deploy it** — `DeploymentExecutor` reads the workspace and copies every file into the server directory (or SFTPs it to Wings).

So your ~617 MB gets written/re-read roughly **3 times**, plus mod downloads have connection overhead per file (DNS + TLS handshake + HTTP round trip each, serialized). That's why after the bar hits 100% of the download there's visibly "hours of work" — it's disk I/O and network, not a hang.

## What would make it much faster

**Option A — structural (biggest win):** have the CurseForge/Modrinth providers return a **ready-to-deploy directory** instead of a rebuilt zip. That eliminates step 1 *and* step 2 entirely:
- overrides get extracted once directly from the client pack into the package dir,
- mods download straight into that dir,
- then it goes straight to deploy.
- Net effect: ~1.8 GB of disk churn becomes ~600 MB. That's the real "much much faster."

  Cost: touches the provider contract, the orchestrator, workspace/extractor, tests, and the mock providers. Medium-high risk, needs careful validation (the security checks that currently run on the zip need to run on the dir).

**Option B — parallel mod downloads (contained):** the downloader currently fetches mods serially. Using a curl multi-handle to fetch e.g. 8–16 at once would cut the mod-fetch phase by roughly 5–10× for packs with many mods. Contained to `DownloadManager` + how providers feed it destinations. Lower risk, still real work (progress-offset math and retries get trickier).

**Option C — free already done:** the new `StoredZipWriter` (no compression) removed the biggest single dead-zone; the remaining time is now pure I/O/network.

My recommendation: **do A now** (it's the actual answer to your question — you'll feel the difference immediately on a 617 MB pack), then **B** as a follow-up for huge packs. Both are sizeable changes — which would you like me to build? If you want, I can start with A and keep B as a second step.

<?php

namespace Pterodactyl\BlueprintFramework\Extensions\modpackinstaller\Services\Server;

interface ServerFileTarget
{
    public function exists(string $relativePath): bool;

    public function isDirectory(string $relativePath): bool;

    public function read(string $relativePath): string;

    public function write(string $relativePath, string $contents): void;

    /**
     * Copies a local source file into the target, streaming the bytes so that
     * arbitrarily large files can be moved without buffering them in memory.
     */
    public function putFile(string $relativePath, string $sourcePath): void;

    /**
     * Copies a target file out to a local destination path, streaming the
     * bytes so that arbitrarily large files never have to fit in memory.
     */
    public function getFile(string $relativePath, string $destinationPath): void;

    public function delete(string $relativePath): void;

    /** Returns true only when the directory exists and contains no entries. */
    public function isEmptyDirectory(string $relativePath): bool;

    /**
     * Removes a directory that is currently empty. Implementations MUST NOT
     * recurse or tolerate a non-empty directory: callers check emptiness first.
     */
    public function removeDirectory(string $relativePath): void;

    public function ensureDirectory(string $relativePath): void;
}
